summary: the fusion diversification multiplier is sized by the concentration of the weights actually used rather than the source count: DM = 1/sqrt(sum(w^2) + rho(1-sum(w^2))) over the normalised weights, i.e. the same formula at the inverse-Herfindahl effective number of sources — identical to the old rule at equal weights, never larger than it, and never below 1, so a source held at the MIN floor for measured-negative expectancy no longer buys a full extra unit of diversification leverage (ADR-0076)
